question: does IAM refuse a valid credential whose principal has no grant?
principal: recall-sa-controller (secret access, NO run.invoker on the gateway)
expected_reason: forbidden (authenticated, no grant for this principal)
observed_reason: forbidden (authenticated, no grant for this principal)
body_excerpt:
Error: Forbidden

Your client does not have permission to get URL /v1

revocation_proof.behavioural: impersonation attempted repeatedly until it FAILED
revocation_proof.lag_observed: The policy read-back reported the binding removed while impersonation STILL SUCCEEDED for four further attempts; the mint was refused on the fifth. Grant propagation showed the same lag in reverse: the binding was present for two attempts before a token could be minted.
revocation_proof.why_both_are_recorded: Reading the policy back is stronger than trusting the remove call, and it is still a control-plane assertion standing in for behaviour -- the same shape as every other defect found in this work. A revoked binding is not immediately an unusable one. The policy is the intent; the behaviour is the fact, and only the behaviour closes the privilege window.

what_this_answers: IAM DOES perform the authorization work. A Google-signed token with the correct audience, from a principal confirmed by sub==uniqueId to be recall-sa-controller and holding no run.invoker on this service, was refused 403 by Cloud Run IAM before reaching the container. This is the counterpart to the audience finding: the perimeter does not decide on audience, but it does decide on grant.
